review.intent_summary: Expose causal native historical anomaly evidence through one opt-in forecast call while leaving business materiality, severity and notifications under consumer control.

criteria.criterion: 1. Reuse historical analysis, preserve original positions and calibrate against the frozen selected baseline.
2. Preserve earlier points and first-detection patterns across suffix changes, prevent provisional triggers and separate retrospective screening.
3. Preserve default forecasts, signed decomposition, horizon prefixes and adjustment semantics; fail without partial evidence.
4. Provide public schemas, a single-call adapter and migration guidance for independent selection, materiality, baseline labels and version negotiation without changing Guard or notifications.
criteria.notes: Schemas, adapter and consumer boundaries are implemented, but the migration guide says the example now pins 0.8.0 while the actual adapter pins 0.9.1; reconcile the current adoption instructions.

verification_evidence: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_forecast_anomalies.py tests/test_recent_level.py — Python 3.12.9; 56 passed.
Manual source review confirmed signed versus display references, selected-baseline calibration/readiness, first-detection snapshots and separation of statistical qualification from business severity.
remaining_gaps: Update migration guidance to identify the current 0.9.1 adapter pin and its relationship to the capability's 0.8.0 release prerequisite.
Published-artifact provenance, clean wheel/sdist verification and offline Linux Python 3.12 Lambda execution were not established in this review.
Consumer enablement still requires separately reviewed UsageTap adoption using a verified published artifact.
